# Benchmark cost vs accuracy — Claude triage agents on the 147-gene bench

## Figure legend — Supplementary Figure 3

*Verbatim from the manuscript. Generated by
`scripts/figures/sync_readme_legends.py` — edit the manuscript and
re-run; do not hand-edit inside these markers.*

> **Supplementary Figure 3.** Across model tiers and amounts of supplied context, triage accuracy saturates near 98% well before cost does, so the cheapest configuration reaching that plateau is the economical production choice. Each point is one model–context combination, as in Supplementary Figure 2. The horizontal axis is the projected cost of triaging all 19,324 protein-coding genes once (log scale); the vertical axis is mean soft-credit accuracy on SurfaceBench. Cost is built from average tokens sent and returned per call at Anthropic’s October 2026 list prices, with shared instructions charged once at the first-use rate and reused cheaply, and each web search billed at one cent. Moving from Sonnet 4.6 to Opus 4.8 costs roughly 1.8 times as much for 0.7 percentage points, and adding a search tool costs more than moving to Opus — the two web-search configurations are among the three most expensive points on the chart. Production uses Sonnet 4.6 with identifiers, which came within 0.7 percentage points of Opus 4.8 at the lowest cost among the models available when the pipeline was built; of the later Claude 5.5 models, Haiku 5.5 came within a point of it at about a fourteenth of the cost, and Sonnet 5.5 was the most accurate configuration tested. Refused calls are excluded from accuracy and the refusal rate is labeled (about 5% for Opus 5.5 at its default reasoning effort and 4% at low effort; no other model refused). Color indicates model generation. The two lavender points are the production triage configuration and the PubMed-abstract variant used for the rescue lanes.
<!-- END manuscript-legend -->

Each point is one (model, prompt-variant) cell of the triage agent
benchmark. There are 18 cells: Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.6 each ×
{naive, + IDs, + IDs + PubMed, + IDs + web}, Sonnet 5 × {+ IDs},
Opus 4.8 × {naive, + IDs}, Opus 5 × {+ IDs}, Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5
each × {naive, + IDs}, and Opus 5.5 × {+ IDs, + IDs at low reasoning
effort}. "+ IDs" means the prompt carries the gene's resolved
identifiers; "+ PubMed" and "+ web" add a PubMed or web-search tool on
top.

Color encodes model generation (orange Claude 4.x, blue Claude 5, teal
Claude 5.5; darker = larger model or more context), and the two
configurations the production pipeline uses (Sonnet 4.6 + IDs and
+ IDs + PubMed) are lavender. Each label is drawn in a darker shade of
its point's color.

Refused calls — a safety classifier declining to answer, which only Opus
5.5 does on this bench — are excluded from both accuracy and cost, and
the refusal rate is printed in the cell's label.

- **y-axis:** verdict accuracy on the 147-gene labeled bench, as the
  mean over the 3 replicates of each cell, over answered calls. A prediction counts as a
  match under the soft-credit rule used by the bench figures: `yes` or
  `contextual` matches a truth of `yes` or `contextual`; `no` matches
  `no` only.
- **x-axis (log scale):** projected cost of one triage pass (1
  replicate) over all 19,324 protein-coding genes. For each cell the
  script takes the mean tokens per call. The shared system prompt is
  charged once at the cache-write rate and then reused at the
  cache-read rate for every other gene; the rest of the prompt is
  charged at the input rate and the reply at the output rate. Cells
  that recorded no cache tokens are treated as having a 2,000-token
  shared system prompt. Each web search adds $0.01. The per-call cost
  is then multiplied by 19,324. Per-million-token prices are set in the
  `_PRICE` table at the top of the script.

The y-axis floor is max(78%, lowest cell accuracy − 2 points), which
is about 79.6% here, to spread the LLM cells. DB baselines are left
out on purpose (they would squash the LLM cluster against the bottom
of the chart). For the DB-vs-LLM comparison, see
`db_correctness_overall` and `db_correctness_by_class`.

Run:

```
uv run make_benchmark_cost_vs_accuracy.py
```

Data: the bundled `benchmark_cost_vs_accuracy.tsv` next to the script
(no download). It has one row per gene × model × prompt variant ×
replicate, with token counts (prompt, completion, cache write, cache
read), web-search count, the predicted and ground-truth verdicts, and
the soft-credit `is_match` flag. It is built by
`scripts/build_figure_tsvs.py` from
`data/processed/triage_bench/mainbench_replicates_v2.tsv` (exported
from public D1 by `scripts/tsv-export/export_mainbench_to_tsv.py`;
truth labels from `data/eval/triage_benchmark_v1.tsv` and `is_match`
are added by `scripts/figures/augment_figure_tsvs_with_stable_ids.py`).
Outside a gist, the script reads the in-repo copy at
`data/processed/figures/benchmark_cost_vs_accuracy.tsv`.

Canonical in-repo generator:
[`scripts/figures/benchmark_cost_vs_accuracy.py`](https://github.com/Deliverome-Project/accessible-surfaceome/blob/main/scripts/figures/benchmark_cost_vs_accuracy.py).
